extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, IP attorneys, and IP professionals working with ARIPO/ African regional filings
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of procedural and substantive amendments to the ARIPO Harare Protocol affecting patents, utility models and industrial designs (rules on examination, amendments, restoration, publication, divisional applications, biotech, fees, and time extensions). Intended to guide applicants and practitioners filing under ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Protocol provides for post-grant amendments if an Applicant applies in writing and pays the prescribed fee on condition that the amendment falls wholly within the scope of the claims before an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after grant are permitted only when requested in writing, the prescribed fee is paid, and the amended subject-matter does not extend beyond the scope of the originally granted claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination is now required to be requested when filing an ARIPO patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must explicitly request substantive examination at filing (or as prescribed by procedure); failure to request may affect examination and prosecution under ARIPO procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration (reestablishment) of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of a provision for restoration (reestablishment of rights). The condition for restoration is the non-observance of the time limit which was a direct consequence of a refused or withdrawn application. Successful restoration will be published in the ARIPO Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is available where deadlines were missed due to a refused or withdrawn application; applicants must follow restoration procedures and, if granted, the restoration is publicly notified in the ARIPO Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: methods of treatment and multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on drafting claims involving methods of treatment and multiple dependent claims have been included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New rules address how to draft and treat claims directed to therapeutic methods and permit/clarify multiple dependent claim formats according to the Protocol's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnological inventions (Rule 7 and 7bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on biotechnological inventions have been included in Rule 7 and patentable biotechnological inventions and exceptions thereto in 7bis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Protocol now contains specific guidance and defined exceptions for patentability of biotechnological subject-matter under Rules 7 and 7bis, which applicants must consult for biotech filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-month extension period may be applied for if the Applicant requests the same in writing and pays the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can seek a three-month extension to applicable time limits by written request and payment of the prescribed fee; check which deadlines are eligible and the required formality for the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of ARIPO patent applications (18-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of ARIPO patent applications has been introduced. Publication will take place soon after the expiry of 18 months from the date of filing or the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications filed under ARIPO will be published automatically around 18 months from filing/priority; applicants should plan confidentiality, prior publication, and third-party observation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provision on divisional patent applications has been introduced. A divisional application which relates to a pending earlier ARIPO patent application must be filed at the ARIPO office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisionals may be filed at ARIPO for subject-matter of a pending earlier ARIPO application; practitioners should observe timing and formal requirements for filing divisionals with ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in official ARIPO fees
rubrics_metrics.description: There has also been a marked increase in the official fees of the ARIPO Office in respect of patents, industrial designs and utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and agents must budget for higher official fees for filings and procedural steps (patents, designs, utility models) under the amended Protocol; check current fee schedule for exact amounts.
